definitions.explanation: the mental capacity to make sensible decisions and form sound opinions

examples.japanese: {判断力|はんだんりょく}のある{人|ひと}だ。
{緊急時|きんきゅうじ}には{冷静|れいせい}な{判断力|はんだんりょく}が{求|もと}められる。
examples.english: In emergencies, calm judgment is required.

examples.japanese: {疲|つか}れていると{判断力|はんだんりょく}が{鈍|にぶ}る。
examples.english: When you're tired, your judgment becomes impaired.

notes:
FORMS:
{判断|はんだん} (judgment, decision) + {力|りょく} (power, ability) → power of judgment

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {判断力|はんだんりょく}がある (to have good judgment)
- {判断力|はんだんりょく}が{鈍|にぶ}る (judgment becomes dull)
- {判断力|はんだんりょく}に{欠|か}ける (to lack judgment)
- {冷静|れいせい}な{判断力|はんだんりょく} (calm judgment)

RELATED ～{力|りょく} COMPOUNDS:
- {決断力|けつだんりょく} (decisiveness - ability to make firm decisions)
- {洞察力|どうさつりょく} (insight)
- {観察力|かんさつりょく} (observation skills)

LEGAL CONTEXT:
In Japanese law, {判断力|はんだんりょく} is important in determining mental capacity for contracts, wills, etc.
